title: A long-lived Store never sees another process's writes
description: Store connects with LanceDB's default read_consistency_interval=None (store.py), and the MCP server keeps one Store for its lifetime. Verified 2026-10-12 by two independent runs: after another process added or re-pathed a source, the resident handle kept returning the old list_sources, chunk_count and search results until it wrote something itself. Replaying what its next sync would then plan (replace_source at the new path, delete_source at the old) left 400 rows with 200 distinct ids. A terminal 'minirag-mcp sync' beside a running server has this flaw today; the inbox watcher (minirag-mcp-ab4) makes it routine. Fix verified in the same runs: read_consistency_interval=timedelta(0), or table.checkout_latest() before a read; measured cost 0.5 to 0.9 ms per read on a small table. Needs a test that fails without the fix: two Store handles on one directory, write through one, read through the other.
notes: 2026-10-16: fixed on branch fix/sync-and-store-safety, PR #17 (not merged yet). Close after merge.
close_reason: Merged in PR #17 (439b454).

title: sync deletes every indexed source under a root that is unreadable or missing
description: scan_roots uses os.walk with the default onerror, so a root that is missing, chmod 000, or (on macOS) denied by TCC yields zero entries and no error. compute_diff then sees every indexed source under that root as absent from the scan and puts it in to_delete. Verified 2026-10-12 against the real functions on a throwaway root: unreadable root 3 of 3 deleted, unreadable subfolder 3 of 3, missing root 1 of 1. Today a person sees 'deleted: N' on the terminal. An unattended process (the inbox watcher, minirag-mcp-ab4) has nobody watching, and a LaunchAgent denied access to ~/Documents would empty the index. This is the 'silent success' trap in a new place. Fix direction: a root that cannot be listed is a loud error for the whole run, never an empty scan; a subtree that cannot be listed keeps its indexed sources and is reported.
notes:
Also verified 2026-10-12: for a MISSING root with the default DB_PATH, Store.__init__ calls db_path.mkdir(parents=True) and so creates the root and an empty index, then reports all zeros. With DB_PATH elsewhere, or for the second of two roots, every state (chmod 000, EPERM, missing, empty directory left by an unmounted volume) ends in deleted=N and exit 0 on both surfaces. A readability check must list the directory: os.stat and Path.is_dir pass under a TCC-style denial while os.scandir fails with EPERM. An empty directory in the root's place passes every errno check, so the guard also has to hold deletions for a root that lists zero files while the index has sources under it.
2026-10-16: fixed on branch fix/sync-and-store-safety, PR #17 (not merged yet). Close after merge.
close_reason: Merged in PR #17 (439b454).

title: Measure nearest-neighbour folder classification on a real hand-filed corpus
description: The design may not be approved without this. Take the owner's already-filed corpus (736 indexed documents, 40 folders), remove documents one at a time and predict each one's folder from the rest. Report accuracy and the share of confident answers, the risk-coverage trade-off of the confidence rule, behaviour on documents whose folder does not exist (must abstain), and sensitivity to duplicates and near-duplicates. The numbers decide whether neighbours alone are enough or an optional LLM tier is needed.
close_reason: Measured 2026-10-12, reproduced blind through LanceDB and attacked by two reviewers. Rule as specified: 439 of 736 moved, 0 wrong in leave-one-out; 17 of 287 outside the two largest folders; documents with no home misfiled at 0.2 to 4% depending on which folders exist; a local 27B LLM as arbiter 81% precise. Numbers, caveats and method are in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-12-inbox-design.md; scripts and raw output live outside the repository (see bd memories).

title: Embedded images in DOCX and PPTX never reach the index
description:
markitdown renders an embedded picture as ![](data:image/png;base64,...) and parser.strip_data_uri_images removes the placeholder — correct for noise, but it means the picture's content never reaches the index at all.

Measured on the real corpus 2026-08-10: 4819 embedded images across 375 of 543 docx files (plus 30 in pptx). A random sample of 20 images run through the shipped [ocr] tier: 12 of 20 carry more than 200 characters of text, median 716 characters among those — roughly two million characters of searchable content missing from the index. In functional specifications the pictures are not illustrations but the substance: screenshots of 1C forms and tax registers. One sampled spec screenshot yields 'Регистр налогового учета 150 форма', the reporting period, and the code 150.00.026 with its description — none of which appears anywhere in the document's text, so no query can ever reach it.

Cost is small: 20 images took 13 seconds on the fast tier, so the whole corpus is about an hour once, then only changed documents. The engine is already shipped.

Design questions to settle before building: which images are worth OCRing (a size or aspect threshold keeps logos and icons out — 8 of the 20 sampled carried nothing); where the recognized text goes in the markdown (in place of the placeholder, keeping reading order, seems right); whether it should be gated on the [ocr] extra like the rest; and whether the alt text markitdown sometimes carries should be preferred when present. Note the related idea the owner raised earlier: a VLM could describe pictures rather than transcribe them, which is a different feature and belongs to the parked [ocr-max] work.

title: markitdown drops PDF tables when no page trips its form heuristic
description:
markitdown 0.1.7's PDF converter decides per DOCUMENT, not per page. _extract_form_content_from_words returns None for a page unless it looks form-like (needs >=3 aligned columns, avg column width >=30px, <=10 columns/inch, and table rows >=20% of the page's rows). If form_page_count == 0 for the whole document, _pdf_converter falls back to pdfminer.high_level.extract_text for everything, which keeps no structure at all.

Reproduced 2026-08-10 with a synthetic contract page (prose plus a three-row payment table below the 20% threshold): the table reaches the index as orphaned values — 'Due / 1 200 000 / 2 000 000 / 01.09.2026 / 30.11.2026' — with column headers gone and every amount detached from its row. A search for the advance amount can never connect it to the row it belongs to. A mixed document is only saved by luck: one page that does trip the heuristic switches the whole document to the per-page path, where tables survive (verified: 2 prose pages + 1 table page keeps a proper Markdown table).

Docling was evaluated as a replacement and rejected: same 146/196 checklist facts on scanned pages as our own tier (148), 30x slower on a real DOCX (9.8s vs 0.3s) and +1 GB with torch. The fix belongs in our PDF branch instead: we already own per-page machinery built for OCR routing, so route table-like pages through pdfplumber ourselves rather than letting one document-level verdict flatten everything.

title: Sync without the [ocr] extra deletes indexed images from the index
description: scan_roots asks supported_extensions(), which is OCR-gated, so a sync run from an environment without the extra does not see image files; compute_diff then puts every indexed image in to_delete and run_sync deletes them, reporting deleted:N without naming the cause. The corpus silently shrinks; recovery is a re-sync with the extra. Found by the whole-branch merge review of the OCR fast tier (2026-08-09). Fix direction: in compute_diff, never propose deletion for a source whose extension is outside the current whitelist but inside the static SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS|IMAGE_EXTENSIONS union — leave it indexed, or report it distinctly.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #14 (merged 3b3a4f5). zx5: unreadable sources are retained and reported instead of deleted, with a disk-existence check so genuinely deleted files still go. 5qy: the scheme verdict keys off scheme-critical columns only, and a failed migration records which columns it left. 6y7: the second pdfminer pass is skipped when OCR is absent. z9u: measured in throwaway venvs — imdecodemulti first exists in 4.7.0.68, and no wheel before 4.10.0.84 imports under numpy 2, so the floor is now >=4.10.0.84 with all four components.

title: ingest_url: restrict hosts, not only schemes
description: security.check_url_scheme (security.py:28) whitelists http/https but places no restriction on the host. http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ (cloud metadata) and http://localhost:8080/admin both pass. The URL is frequently chosen by an LLM rather than a human, and that LLM may be acting on text from an already-indexed document — a prompt-injection to SSRF path. Consider: block link-local/loopback/private ranges by default, resolve the hostname and check the resolved IP (not just the literal), and offer an opt-out env var for users who deliberately index an internal wiki.
close_reason: Done on branch debts (pushed, not merged)

title: scope: unify prefix semantics between scanner and store
description: Two different meanings of scope in one codebase. scanner._in_scope (scanner.py:89) compares path COMPONENTS (correct). store._scope_clause (store.py:65) uses starts_with(), and list_files filters entries with str.startswith (server.py:251, cli/__init__.py:322) — raw string prefixes. Result: scope='/data/proj' also matches '/data/project-secret/f.md'. Scope is the only mechanism for narrowing what an agent can see, so a surprise here is both a correctness and a confidentiality issue. Fix: make store/list_files use component-wise containment (append a path separator, or reuse a shared helper). Also update the spec, which still describes scope as a post-fusion filter while the code prefilters both vector and FTS sides.

description: sync now reports a folder it cannot list and keeps what is indexed under it (minirag-mcp-32f). title: Prior art: how other tools auto-file documents into folders

title: sync: treat a file that vanished and reappeared with the same sha256 as a move, not delete plus re-ingest
description: When the owner re-files a document by hand (Finder, Obsidian), sync today deletes the old source and re-embeds the new path. Once Store.move_source exists for the inbox, sync can pair a to_delete source with a to_ingest path of equal sha256 and re-path the record instead: no re-embedding, and hand-filing a document the inbox left behind becomes free. Needs care with duplicates (two files of one hash) and with titles when the basename changes.
notes:
Pulled into the scope of the inbox spec (2026-10-12): the measurement showed most documents are left for hand-filing, so the watcher runs sync when an indexed file leaves the inbox, and sync must then re-path a same-hash, same-basename file rather than re-embed it (an OCR document is expensive to read twice). A different basename stays delete plus ingest, because the title can come from the stem.

title: replace_source is two commits: two processes ingesting one source leave duplicate chunks no sync repairs
description: Store.replace_source deletes the source's rows and then adds the new ones, as two separate commits. Verified 2026-10-12 by interleaving those two statements from two handles (sync in one process, ingest_file in another, same file): a 3-chunk file ended with 6 rows, the next sync reported it as skipped because hash and mtime match, and a later re-path returned rows_updated=6. A reader between the two commits also sees the source as absent (44 of 196 racing snapshots). The sync lock does not help: single-file ingest is deliberately unlocked. Fix direction, verified to be one commit in the same session: merge_insert keyed on id with when_not_matched_by_source_delete restricted to the source, so the replacement is atomic and a second writer cannot interleave. Needs a test that goes red on the two-commit version.
notes: 2026-10-16: fixed on branch fix/sync-and-store-safety, PR #17 (not merged yet). Close after merge.
close_reason: Merged in PR #17 (439b454).

title: Index is never compacted: keyword search pays about 50x, vector search about 3x
description: Nothing in src/ calls table.optimize(). replace_source is delete plus add, so a synced index holds one fragment per document and two versions per ingest. Measured on a copy of the real 736-document index (121,419 chunks; 736 fragments, 1,485 versions), idle machine, three runs: vector search top-50 median 31 to 34 ms, one FTS query 246 to 278 ms. After table.optimize() (about 10 s) on the same copy: 1 fragment, vector search 10.3 to 10.6 ms, FTS 4 to 7 ms, results identical. Every hybrid query runs one FTS query, so a search on that corpus pays about a quarter of a second for it. A second investigator found on a synthetic table that the BM25 indexes hold no rows until optimize() runs (indexed=0, unindexed=69000), which is the flat-scan cost above. CORRECTION: the first version of this issue said 392 ms and 540 ms and '25x'; those were measured while other heavy work was running on the machine and are withdrawn. Fix direction: compact at the end of a sync that changed anything, and prune old versions; decide the trigger so a one-file ingest does not pay a full rewrite.
notes: 2026-10-16: since Store reads with read_consistency_interval=0 (fix for 9wf), every read also resolves the latest version, and that cost grows with the versions kept: count_rows overhead about 0.1 ms at 10 versions, 0.7 ms at 1k, 2.5 ms at 5k, 4.7 ms at 10k (measured by the branch review on lancedb 0.36). optimize(cleanup_older_than=...) after a sync would bound both this and the fragment growth.

title: Inbox: drop a document, it is classified, filed and indexed on its own
description: Goal: a file dropped into an inbox folder inside the document root is parsed, classified into one of the EXISTING folders, moved there and indexed, locally, with no agent in the loop and no manual command. Missing today: a trigger (new files are picked up only by sync / sync_start), a classifier (choose the destination folder) and an index-aware move. Owner's design inputs: nearest-neighbour classification over the existing index as the base (no LLM, no new dependency); an LLM through a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint only as an optional second tier; unsure means do not move, and the reason is visible in list and status; never create folders; same sha256 means the index record is re-pathed, not rebuilt; never overwrite, never leave BASE_DIR, move journal with undo, dry-run; tolerate half-written files; cross-platform trigger with one resident process; identical through MCP and CLI. Process: measurement first (leave-one-out on the owner's hand-filed corpus), then spec in docs/superpowers/specs, owner review, plan, TDD. Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-12-inbox-design.md
close_reason: Dropped by the owner on 2026-10-16. Measurement plus prior-art research: auto-filing would move ~3% of real arrivals (5 of 168) on this archive, at the cost of a background service, a file mover, journal and undo, and macOS TCC trouble. Spec branch docs/inbox-spec deleted. What stays: defects 32f, 9wf, 505 and sync re-pathing a hand-moved file (ab4.4).

title: scanner: skip Office lock files (~$ prefix) so an open document does not fail the sync
description: GitHub issue #15. scan_roots skips dot-prefixed names but not the '~$' prefix Word/Excel/PowerPoint use for lock files, so '~$port.docx' passes the whitelist and is handed to markitdown, which raises BadZipFile (the lock file is a small binary blob, not a ZIP). Measured: the run does NOT hang as the report claims — it fails fast (0.04s) and per-file error handling catches it — but every sync of a directory with an open Office document reports failed: N and 'minirag-mcp sync' exits 1. The reported 'scanned stays 0' is unrelated: SyncJob.counts holds its all-zero default until _run_sync_unlocked returns, so a running job always reports zeros.
acceptance_criteria: scan_roots omits names starting with '~$'; a test that goes red against the unfixed scanner; full suite green; issue #15 closed with the corrected diagnosis.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #16 (merged): scan_roots now skips the ~$ prefix. Test goes red on the unfixed scanner; full suite and CI matrix green.

title: A cosmetic added column makes schema_migrated=False lie about scheme staleness
description: _ADDED_COLUMNS was a set of chunking-scheme-critical columns, and schema_migrated=False drives two consequences built on that: stale_chunk_count() returns count_rows() ('the whole index is scheme-stale') and parent_texts() returns {}. ocr_engine is neither. An older index opened where add_columns fails (read-only copy or concurrent writer — both deliberately supported) now warns 'This index predates the current chunking scheme' (false), reports 100% of chunks stale and tells the user to re-sync everything (false), and switches off parent-section retrieval unnecessarily. Found by the whole-branch merge review of the OCR fast tier (2026-08-09). Fix direction: split the map into scheme-critical and additive columns and key schema_migrated (or its two consumers) off only what they need.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #14 (merged 3b3a4f5). zx5: unreadable sources are retained and reported instead of deleted, with a disk-existence check so genuinely deleted files still go. 5qy: the scheme verdict keys off scheme-critical columns only, and a failed migration records which columns it left. 6y7: the second pdfminer pass is skipped when OCR is absent. z9u: measured in throwaway venvs — imdecodemulti first exists in 4.7.0.68, and no wheel before 4.10.0.84 imports under numpy 2, so the floor is now >=4.10.0.84 with all four components.

title: OCR bench: run the fast tier over the full scan corpus on the M5
description: Acceptance bench for the shipped [ocr] tier (the VLM comparison is parked with minirag-mcp-qbz). On the target MacBook Pro M5 64GB, run the entity-checklist bench over all 11 pages of the private scanned test PDF (location in bd memory, key ocr-test-assets) and settle the four questions the design left open: (1) the raised RapidOCR resolution cap vs the default on 300dpi renders — neutral on the 2227px test page but 300dpi PDF renders lose 29%; (2) CLAHE gated by a low-contrast metric — the degradation stand measured +1 on a clean scan, +4 on the worst degraded variant, -1 on noise-only; (3) rapid-orientation accuracy on rotated scan pages before enabling auto-rotate anywhere it is not already; (4) CoreML execution provider vs plain CPU — RapidOCR's tracker warns per-node fallback can make it slower, so enable only on a measured win. Also worth checking: sparse-content pages that OCR to '' at default Det thresholds.
notes: Bench must also A/B (added after preprocessing research): (1) raised RapidOCR resolution cap vs default on 300dpi renders; (2) CLAHE gated by a low-contrast metric (stand: +1 clean, +4 worst-degraded, -1 noise-only); (3) rapid-orientation accuracy on rotated scan pages; (4) CoreML EP vs plain CPU. MEASURED 2026-08-10 on M2 Pro over the 11-page PDF: fast tier 148/196 checklist facts, 18s total. Two things for the M5 run to settle: (a) the PDF is built 1px=1pt, so a 300dpi render upsamples 4x before the engine's 4000px cap downsamples again — on the УПД this UPSAMPLING GAINED 3 facts (24/27 vs 21/27 on the raw bitmap), so the render-scale/cap interaction is worth tuning deliberately; (b) the ЭСФ form page scores 0/15 — the detector finds 109 text regions where the form has hundreds, and the candidate cap (1000) is not the limit, resolution is. A dense-form page may need a higher render scale than the rest.

title: [ocr-max] tier: Qwen3-VL VLM engine, in-process and local-endpoint modes
description: Per the spec: extras ocr-max = torch+transformers+accelerate plus mlx-vlm under a darwin/arm64 marker; default model Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct (RAG_OCR_MODEL; 30B-A3B-Instruct as 64GB ceiling). In-process is the primary path: MLX quant on Apple Silicon (pin exact community build after a smoke test), torch with RAG_OCR_DEVICE auto cuda->mps->cpu elsewhere (loud resolution, hard error on unavailable explicit device). Local OpenAI-compatible endpoint (RAG_OCR_ENDPOINT, requests-only, health-check) is an optional escape hatch, not a requirement; when it points at ollama request num_ctx>=16384, treat done_reason=length as an error, and use the -instruct tag (bare tag is a thinking checkpoint returning empty content). Strip markdown fence; blank-page guard; document handwriting-hallucination limitation.
notes: PARKED by owner decision 2026-08-09. Measured evidence, updated 2026-08-10 over the 11-page scanned PDF (196 checklist facts): fast RapidOCR 148, docling+RapidOCR 146, docling+Qwen3-VL-8B 170, Qwen3-VL-8B alone 173, claude -p Sonnet 5 192, Opus 5 194. Two findings that matter if this ever resumes: (1) the input resolution cap costs facts — the VLM read 27/27 on the УПД at full resolution and 23/27 at a 3 Mpx render, where it produced fluent corruptions ('Химреактивнашаб', a dropped digit in a 12-digit БИН); (2) pairing docling's VLM pipeline with the same local model buys the document structure at almost the same accuracy (170 vs 173) — on the dense ЭСФ form docling recovered 13 tables. For a corpus made entirely of scans that pairing, not a bare VLM, is the architecture to start from. Trap seen for the third time: docling talks to ollama over the OpenAI-compatible endpoint where num_ctx cannot be passed, so pages silently returned empty documents with ConversionStatus.SUCCESS until the server was restarted with OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH.

title: [ocr] tier: RapidOCR fallback for scanned PDFs and image files
description: Per the spec: extras ocr = rapidocr+onnxruntime+pypdfium2; per-page pdfminer char counts route pages below RAG_OCR_MIN_CHARS_PER_PAGE (default 25) to OCR; eslav default via RAG_OCR_LANG (stock ch/en model silently drops Cyrillic; model_type=mobile is the ceiling — no server Cyrillic model exists); model files in <base_dir>/ocr-models, never site-packages; CoreML EP auto on macOS (measure before advertising); image extensions join SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS only when OCR active; loud errors for missing extra / failed model download; reading-order paragraph assembly from line boxes; ocr:<engine> marker on chunk records.
notes: Preprocessing decisions (spec section 'Image preparation before OCR', researched+measured 2026-08-09): render 300dpi with Global.max_side_len=4000 + Det.limit_type=max + Det.limit_side_len=1600 (engine otherwise silently resamples to 2000px and crops rec from the downscaled image); rapid-orientation (Apache-2.0, 6.5MB ONNX, same ort+opencv stack) confidence-gated for 0/90/180/270 + EXIF-blind cv2 loads; no binarization/denoise/deskew (measured harmful or useless on DL engines); BGR ndarray straight into engine, no intermediate files.
close_reason: Shipped: [ocr] tier merged in PR #13 and released as v0.5.0. RapidOCR eslav on onnxruntime + pypdfium2 + rapid-orientation behind the optional extra; per-page PDF routing, image files as documents (incl. multi-page TIFF), ocr_engine marker through store/CLI/MCP, loud failure without the extra. 495 tests green extra-free, 7 slow with the real engine, smoke on a real 11-page scan: 76 chunks, [ocr:rapidocr]. Follow-ups: minirag-mcp-zx5, -5qy, -6y7, -z9u.

title: Avoid embedding every chunk twice per ingest
description: Pipeline._chunk_and_store embeds twice: once inside merge_blocks (pipeline.py:101, block granularity, for the similarity merge decision) and again for the final chunks (pipeline.py:109). Any block that survives unmerged is embedded twice — roughly 2x the ingest cost, which is the dominant cost on a large corpus (558 docs took 35 min). Fix needs merge_blocks to return (text, vector) pairs instead of list[str], reusing the vectors it already computed for chunks that were not merged; merged chunks still need a fresh vector.

title: Strip image placeholders from ingested markdown
description: Measured on a real 558-document corpus: 4442 of 52231 chunks (8.5%) contain markitdown image placeholders like ![](data:image/png;base64...) — 0.9% of all indexed characters. Harmless for ranking but noisy in query results and read_file output, and one boilerplate-heading case was actually an image placeholder acting as the H1 (already handled in parser._is_usable_heading). Strip data: image links during parsing, keeping any alt text.

title: Ship the leave-one-out replay as a command, so each owner can calibrate the inbox thresholds on their own corpus
description: The inbox defaults (margin 0.70, closeness 0.80) were measured on one private corpus with the default embedding model. A public package should let any owner see, on their own index, how many documents the rule would file and how many wrongly, before turning the watcher on. The measurement is cheap on a compacted index: 16 vector searches per document. Report forced accuracy, moved share and wrong moves at the configured thresholds, by folder size, plus the chronological replay. Not part of the first version; the dry run covers the immediate need.
close_reason: Dropped by the owner on 2026-10-16. Measurement plus prior-art research: auto-filing would move ~3% of real arrivals (5 of 168) on this archive, at the cost of a background service, a file mover, journal and undo, and macOS TCC trouble. Spec branch docs/inbox-spec deleted. What stays: defects 32f, 9wf, 505 and sync re-pathing a hand-moved file (ab4.4).

title: Check whether FastMCP's start banner contacts pypi.org
description: README says no network I/O happens besides ingest_url and the one-time model download. An investigator read .venv/.../fastmcp/utilities/version_check.py, which queries https://pypi.org/pypi/fastmcp/json by default, and saw 'Update available: 4.1.0' on the server's stderr, though that line may have come from a cache. Not verified with a network capture. If the call happens, disable it at startup (FastMCP has a setting for it) and add a test that the server starts with the network unreachable; if it does not, record why and close.

title: CLI and MCP disagree on two error paths
description: Parity between the two shells is a convention with no mechanical check, and two cases have drifted (verified by running both, 2026-10-12). With an unusable DB_PATH, MCP status returns indexError while CLI status dies with a FileExistsError traceback (_load catches three exception types only). CLI 'query ""' returns hits with exit 0 while MCP raises 'query must not be empty'. Fix both in the core so the shells cannot differ, and consider one parametrised test that runs each capability through both surfaces.

title: Verify the opencv-python floor that cv2.imdecodemulti needs
description: The [ocr] extra pins opencv-python>=4.5.5 because ocr.ocr_image uses cv2.imdecodemulti for multi-page images, but the behavior was only ever run against the resolved 5.0.0.93 — the declared floor itself is untested. This is the project's own documented trap ('no difference on the interpreters I have' is not 'no difference on the versions we support'). Failure mode is loud (AttributeError surfacing as OcrError), not silent, so this is low priority: install opencv-python==4.5.5 in a scratch env, confirm imdecodemulti exists and returns (ok, frames), and raise the floor if it does not.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #14 (merged 3b3a4f5). zx5: unreadable sources are retained and reported instead of deleted, with a disk-existence check so genuinely deleted files still go. 5qy: the scheme verdict keys off scheme-critical columns only, and a failed migration records which columns it left. 6y7: the second pdfminer pass is skipped when OCR is absent. z9u: measured in throwaway venvs — imdecodemulti first exists in 4.7.0.68, and no wheel before 4.10.0.84 imports under numpy 2, so the floor is now >=4.10.0.84 with all four components.

title: Every PDF ingest now pays a second full pdfminer pass
description: parser._pdf_with_ocr_fallback calls ocr.pdf_page_texts for per-page character counts, and markitdown's PDF converter is itself pdfminer/pdfplumber-based, so a text PDF is parsed twice on every ingest. Unmeasured sync-time regression on the most common path (558-document corpus). Note that when OCR is unavailable the pass buys nothing markdown.strip() cannot answer, so short-circuiting there removes the cost entirely for default installs. Measure on the real corpus before optimizing — pair with the OCR bench task.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #14 (merged 3b3a4f5). zx5: unreadable sources are retained and reported instead of deleted, with a disk-existence check so genuinely deleted files still go. 5qy: the scheme verdict keys off scheme-critical columns only, and a failed migration records which columns it left. 6y7: the second pdfminer pass is skipped when OCR is absent. z9u: measured in throwaway venvs — imdecodemulti first exists in 4.7.0.68, and no wheel before 4.10.0.84 imports under numpy 2, so the floor is now >=4.10.0.84 with all four components.

title: OCR docs: README install/config section for [ocr] and [ocr-max]
description: Document: uvx --from 'minirag-mcp[ocr]' invocation; UV_TORCH_BACKEND note for Linux CPU users of [ocr-max] (pip extras cannot select wheel indexes; default Linux torch pulls CUDA multi-GB); ollama path as the recommended Apple Silicon route (ollama pull qwen3-vl:8b-instruct + RAG_OCR_ENDPOINT); config surface RAG_OCR_ENGINE/RAG_OCR_LANG/RAG_OCR_MODEL/RAG_OCR_DEVICE/RAG_OCR_ENDPOINT/RAG_OCR_MIN_CHARS_PER_PAGE; handwriting-hallucination caveat; never install onnxruntime-gpu alongside (import-name conflict, silent CPU fallback).
close_reason: Done for what shipped: the README gained a full 'OCR for scanned documents' section in v0.5.0 (install, per-page routing, image extensions, ocrEngine surface, both new env vars in the settings table, an honest quality note), and CLAUDE.md gained the uv sync --exact gotcha. The [ocr-max] half of this issue is parked with minirag-mcp-qbz and belongs to it if that tier is ever built.

title: Reindex the solidcore corpus with current code
description: The working index under scratchpad (built 2026-08-07) predates the title-precedence fixes in 1bb475c: titles there come from 9f43457's rule, which preferred the filename even when a real H1 existed. An offline re-measurement showed the final rule differs on only 7 of 558 documents, so this is low urgency — but any real use of that corpus should start from a fresh sync with current code. Note DB_PATH defaults to <root>/.minirag/lancedb, i.e. inside the documents folder; pass --db-path explicitly to keep the index elsewhere.
close_reason: Dropped by owner decision: title-rule delta is 7 of 558 documents, reindex not worth it

title: Publish to PyPI so uvx minirag-mcp works
description: The package is installable only via uvx --from git+https://github.com/sfrangulov/minirag-mcp. Publishing to PyPI shortens every install snippet in the README and in MCP client configs. Needs: name availability check, a trusted-publisher or API-token setup, a release workflow, and a README pass to switch the snippets back to the short form.
close_reason: Done: minirag-mcp 0.4.1 is live on PyPI (summary and version match this repo's v0.4.1 release), README snippets already use the short 'uvx minirag-mcp' form, release workflow exists in .github/workflows

title: Narrow the open_table exception handler
description: store.py:138-139 catches bare Exception around open_table and treats any failure as table-missing, then calls create_table. A corrupt table or a permissions error is therefore misreported as a confusing create-time error instead of the real cause. Narrow to the not-found error (ValueError in lancedb 0.36) and let other failures surface. Small related cleanups: delete_source (store.py:225) materializes rows just to count them — use count_rows(filter=...); ingest_file (pipeline.py:135,149) stats the file twice — capture one stat result.
close_reason: Done on branch debts (pushed, not merged)

title: Deferred: ingest_url tool (server-side web fetch)
description: Server fetches URL itself and extracts main content. Deferred from v1 by user decision (2026-08-07). Implementation note (verified 2026-08-07): markitdown ships convert_url()/convert_uri() plus special converters for YouTube/Wikipedia/RSS out of the box, so fetching is nearly free — combine with trafilatura for main-content extraction of generic pages. Keep the offline-after-model-download privacy promise clear in docs if this ships.
close_reason: Folded into v1 by user decision 2026-08-07: ingest_url is in the v1 spec (markitdown convert_url, http/https whitelist)
